label: Browser tab title
context: The title in the browser tab and in search results for the new changelog page at carlosframework.com/platform/changelog.
notes: Matches the platform page's title pattern.

label: Search description
text: 🤖 Every release of the CARLOS platform, every change that landed in it, and who did the work.
context: The summary search engines show under the page title. The site marks AI-written text with a robot, including here, as the platform page does.

label: Link preview description
text: Every release of the CARLOS platform, every change that landed in it, and who did the work.
context: The summary shown when someone pastes the link into Slack or social media.

label: Headline
context: The big heading at the top of the page, under the site's navigation.

label: Introduction
text: Every release of the platform, newest first. Under each release's notes is every change that landed in it: one line per merged branch, linked to its branch and discussions on Amadan, where the platform is developed, and naming the people and agents who did the work.
context: The paragraph under the headline. It tells a reader what each part of the page is: the releases, their notes, and the list of changes under each, and where the links go.

label: Small print about the change lines
text: The change lines are quoted from the history as they were written. Every change from v0.19.0 on links to its branch. Before that, most work was merged on GitHub, where the repository is private, so those changes link only to their commit.
context: Smaller text under the introduction. It explains why the change lines read like commit messages (they are), and why older releases have fewer links.
notes: Facts: every change from v0.19.0 on has a branch link; before that most do not.

label: Release list label (for screen readers)
context: Not shown on screen. Screen readers announce it for the row of release numbers that jump down the page.

label: Link to the published release
context: Beside each release's date, linking to its page on GitHub releases, where the full notes and the binaries are.

label: Release that was never published
context: Shown instead of the link above for the two versions (v0.2.0 and v0.22.1) that were tagged but never released.

label: Fold for older release notes
context: Older releases (before v0.19.0) have long free-form notes, folded away. This is the label you click to open them.

label: Changes heading
context: The heading above each release's list of changes, followed by how many there are.

label: No changes
context: Shown under Changes for a release that added nothing new. No release shows it today, but a re-tag would.

label: Fold for long change lists
context: A release with more than 25 changes shows the first 25 and folds the rest. This is the label, with the number of hidden changes in place of {n}.

label: Credit joiner
context: Joins a person and the agents who worked with them in each change's credit line: "Paul Campbell with claude, codex".

label: Link to the changelog
text: What changed in each release, and who did the work, is in the changelog.
context: A new line in the footer of carlosframework.com/platform, the only link to the changelog from elsewhere on the site.
notes: Keep the link markup around the word you want linked.

label: Release recipe step 10
text: **Changelog.** In a full checkout of `main`, with `gh` and `amadan` signed in, run `git fetch origin --tags '+refs/amadan/closed/*:refs/amadan/closed/*'`, then `go run ./cmd/changelog`. Map each of the new release's bullets to the branches behind it in `docs/site/changelog-links.json`, keyed by the bullet's bold lead, and run it again. Land `docs/site/changelog.json` and the links file on a branch. Then, in `carlosframework/website`, run `node hack/sync-docs.mjs <checkout>` and ship the site the way its AGENTS.md describes. The page is carlosframework.com/platform/changelog.
context: A new last step in the platform README's "Releasing the platform" recipe, which operators follow to cut a release. It says how to update the changelog after a release is published.
